title: MetoHash: A Memory-Efficient and Traffic-Optimized Hashing Index on Hybrid PMem-DRAM Memories
problem: Existing hashing indexes for persistent memory (PMem) suffer from traffic amplification and memory inefficiency due to suboptimal data management across the memory hierarchy.
motivation: PMem offers new opportunities for data-intensive applications but requires careful design to avoid amplifying traffic between fast and slow memory tiers, which can negate performance benefits.
method: MetoHash uses a three-layer index structure: (1) CPU caches for fast inserts, (2) DRAM for arrangement, (3) PMem for persistence. Aggregates key-value items in caches before DRAM arrangement and PMem flush. Uses fingerprinting to reduce unnecessary PMem probing and eliminates duplicates during bucket relocations.
key_novelty: Three-layer index structure with staged insertion and traffic-aware fingerprinting for hybrid PMem-DRAM systems.
contributions: 86.1-257.6% throughput improvement over state-of-the-art PMem hashing indexes
Traffic amplification elimination through staged insertion
Fingerprinting-based optimization for reduced PMem probing
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Specific workload details not provided. Scalability to very large datasets not discussed.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient indexing for hybrid persistent memory systems
